Fanø is a Danish municipality evaluated in the 2022–2023 Annual Report from the Database for Atrial Fibrillation in Denmark (AFDK), published by the Regions' Clinical Quality Development Programme (RKKP). The report assesses the clinical quality of atrial fibrillation treatment across all 98 Danish municipalities, with a specific focus on anticoagulation therapy, safety monitoring, and the prevention of ischemic strokes. 

In the context of Indicator 4b, which measures compliance with safety practices regarding the use of Direct Oral Anticoagulant (DOAC) medications, Fanø achieved an exceptional compliance rate. The municipality met the standard for Indicator 4b with a 99.1% success rate (109 out of 110 eligible cases), resulting in a "Ja" (Yes) designation for meeting the target [^src1]. This 99.1% proportion is the highest recorded among all municipalities in the report, with a 95% confidence interval of 95.0–100.0 [^src1]. 

Conversely, Fanø's performance on other clinical indicators detailed later in the report—such as early initiation of anticoagulation or stroke prevention—was significantly lower. For the metric evaluated on page 94, Fanø did not meet the standard, receiving a "Nej" (No) designation [^src2]. The recorded proportion for this indicator was just 2.2% (with a confidence interval of 0.5–6.3), and specific numerator and denominator counts were suppressed (marked with "#") due to low patient volumes [^src2]. 

This contrast highlights the decentralized nature of healthcare quality in Denmark, where a municipality like Fanø can lead the nation in DOAC safety monitoring while simultaneously struggling with other aspects of atrial fibrillation treatment coverage.
